title: Photosynthesis
text: Photosynthesis is the process by which plants, algae and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy stored in glucose. In plants it takes place in the chloroplasts, which contain the green pigment chlorophyll. The process has two main stages. In the light-dependent reactions, which occur in the thylakoid membranes, chlorophyll absorbs sunlight and uses it to split water molecules, releasing oxygen as a by-product and producing the energy carriers ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle, which occurs in the stroma, the plant uses ATP and NADPH to fix carbon dioxide from the air into sugar molecules. The overall reaction combines carbon dioxide and water, in the presence of light, to produce glucose and oxygen. The rate of photosynthesis depends on light intensity, carbon dioxide concentration and temperature. Photosynthesis is essential for life on Earth because it produces the oxygen we breathe and forms the base of most food chains.
reference_summary: Photosynthesis lets plants convert light into chemical energy stored as glucose, inside chloroplasts. Light-dependent reactions split water and make ATP, NADPH and oxygen, while the Calvin cycle fixes carbon dioxide into sugar. It depends on light, carbon dioxide and temperature, and supplies oxygen and food.

title: Supply and Demand
text: The model of supply and demand explains how prices are determined in a competitive market. The law of demand states that, all else being equal, as the price of a good rises, the quantity demanded falls. The law of supply states that as the price rises, the quantity that producers are willing to supply increases. The demand curve therefore slopes downward and the supply curve slopes upward. The point where the two curves intersect is the market equilibrium, which gives the equilibrium price and quantity. At this price the amount consumers want to buy equals the amount producers want to sell. If the price is above equilibrium, a surplus occurs and sellers lower prices. If the price is below equilibrium, a shortage occurs and prices tend to rise. Shifts in the curves are caused by factors other than price, such as consumer income, tastes, input costs and technology, and they move the equilibrium to a new point.
reference_summary: Supply and demand determine market prices: demand falls and supply rises as price increases. Their curves meet at the equilibrium price and quantity. Surpluses push prices down and shortages push them up, and changes in income, tastes, costs or technology shift the curves and the equilibrium.

title: Newton's Laws of Motion
text: Newton's three laws of motion form the foundation of classical mechanics. The first law, also called the law of inertia, states that an object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion continues moving at constant velocity unless acted on by a net external force. The second law states that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass, which is written as force equals mass times acceleration. This means that a heavier object needs a larger force to achieve the same acceleration. The third law states that for every action there is an equal and opposite reaction. When one body exerts a force on a second body, the second body exerts a force of equal size and opposite direction on the first. Examples include a rocket pushing exhaust gases downward while the gases push the rocket upward, and a person pushing against a wall while the wall pushes back.
reference_summary: Newton's laws underpin classical mechanics. Objects keep their state of motion unless a net force acts on them, acceleration equals net force divided by mass, and every action has an equal and opposite reaction, as seen in rockets and when pushing a wall.

title: Gradient Descent
text: Gradient descent is an optimization algorithm used to train machine learning models by minimizing a loss function. The loss function measures how far the predictions of a model are from the true values. At each step, the algorithm computes the gradient of the loss with respect to the model parameters, which points in the direction of steepest increase, and then updates the parameters by moving a small step in the opposite direction. The size of this step is controlled by the learning rate. If the learning rate is too small, training is slow, and if it is too large, the algorithm may overshoot the minimum or diverge. Batch gradient descent uses the whole training set for each update, stochastic gradient descent uses a single example, and mini-batch gradient descent uses a small group of examples, which is the most common choice in practice. For non-convex problems such as neural networks, gradient descent may settle in local minima or saddle points, so techniques like momentum and adaptive learning rates are often used.
reference_summary: Gradient descent trains models by repeatedly moving parameters opposite the loss gradient, with the learning rate controlling step size. Batch, stochastic and mini-batch variants differ in data used per update, and momentum or adaptive rates help on non-convex problems like neural networks.

title: Causes of the French Revolution
text: The French Revolution, which began in 1789, resulted from a combination of social, economic and political pressures. French society was divided into three estates: the clergy, the nobility and everyone else, known as the Third Estate. The Third Estate made up the vast majority of the population yet bore most of the tax burden, while the first two estates enjoyed privileges and exemptions. France was also in a severe financial crisis, caused by costly wars, including support for the American Revolution, and by an inefficient tax system. Poor harvests in the late 1780s raised the price of bread and left many urban workers and peasants hungry. At the same time, Enlightenment thinkers such as Voltaire, Rousseau and Montesquieu promoted ideas of liberty, equality and popular sovereignty that challenged the absolute monarchy. When King Louis XVI called the Estates-General in 1789 to address the crisis, disputes over voting led the Third Estate to declare itself a National Assembly, and the revolution began.
reference_summary: The French Revolution of 1789 grew from an unequal three-estate system in which the Third Estate paid most taxes, a financial crisis caused by war and poor taxation, food shortages, and Enlightenment ideas of liberty. Disputes in the Estates-General led the Third Estate to form a National Assembly.
